background_notes.fact: For I=[0,1] in ℝ with its usual metric d(x,y)=|x−y|, the open ball B(1/2,1/4) is contained in I, and 1/2∈interior(I); in particular interior(I) is nonempty.

grounds.reason: Specifies the center 1/2 and positive radius 1/4 in the real line.

background_notes.justification: For any point x of that ball, |x−1/2|<1/4 gives −1/4<x−1/2<1/4 and hence 1/4<x<3/4. Therefore 0≤x≤1. The radius is positive and the center lies in its ball. In a metric space an interior point is precisely a point with an open ball of positive radius contained in the set; metric balls are open by the triangle inequality.

background_notes.fact: The real line with norm |·| and real scalar multiplication is a finite dimensional real normed space, and finrank_ℝ(ℝ)=1.

grounds.reason: Defines finrank as the cardinality of a finite basis.

background_notes.justification: The absolute value on the real field is a norm: it is nonnegative, vanishes exactly at zero, satisfies |a x|=|a||x| and |x+y|≤|x|+|y|. These identities follow from ordered-field absolute value (the triangle inequality follows by bounding x+y between −(|x|+|y|) and |x|+|y|). Its scalar and additive operations give the usual real normed space. Each x∈ℝ is x·1, proving span, while c·1=0 implies c=0, proving independence of the singleton. It is therefore a finite basis with cardinality one, giving both finite dimensionality and the stated finrank.
